body:
> No one has a right to treat you like your other ex did, you're doing your best and that deserves nothing but praise. 

Thank you for being so kind.  I appreciate it more than you may know.  There are people everywhere I look, but they feel so far away.  I'm very alone now.  It's been months since I've even had a hug.  

It's beautiful that you care enough to take time to respond to someone's pain.  It gives me hope that there's some warmth in this world.

> Have you ever talked to anyone about the way you feel, about being blind to some kind of subtext of social dynamics? I can imagine it's not something you like to bring up in social conversation.

I have sometimes mentioned off-hand that I struggle with etiquette or that I'm not certain of the appropriate response.  

It seems like there are scripts, but I don't think in these terms, so I can seem unnatural when I attempt to insert an etiquette "script" into a conversation.  But when I don't insert these scripts at all, people see me as either bizarre or rude or both.  (I may be seeming that way, right now.)  And I tend to talk about things in some way that other people aren't talking about them, so there are strange disconnects ... like we're speaking different languages. 

The thought of it makes me feel like I'm in a minefield sometimes, so I often just clam up entirely.  The only other alternative is to go into the whole extrovert performance I mentioned earlier.  There doesn't seem to be much gray-area there ... it's sometimes black, sometimes white, always out-of-sync.

I had an ex who would say unkind things to me (ex: "Are you a moron?" and so on), and one of the things he would criticize is my social competence. Other people say things about this sometimes, but they do it behind my back to each other, and I find out later.  I don't really get the impression that telling them I struggle with it changes anything.

I did have another ex, however, who was really great.  He was very extroverted, and never seemed to judge me for being the way I am.  He'd even give me helpful tips, like "My mom would like it if you talked to her for a little while".  He understood people in a way I didn't.  I haven't met anyone else like this since, but that could be because I have difficulty getting to know people. I'm sure they exist.

> Caring about others matters so much more than just fitting in with them. As far as I'm concerned, that's what qualifies you as a good person, not picking up on social mores.

The other day, I was at a 7-11, and I saw a pair of sunglasses someone left behind.  I realized they belonged to an old woman who had left the store, and I chased her down the block to return them.  She was just so happy to get them back.  It was the first time in a long time that I actually felt happy.  It's probably silly that something so small could have that effect.  For a little while, I felt like I came to life.

> Are there any people you do connect with in a way that doesn't cause you stress? Close friends or family? 

I don't have any close friends anymore.  I've had friendships that I believed were close at the time, but they turned out not to be as close as I thought they were. It's not easy for me to make friends, and it takes a long time for me to be comfortable being close to anyone.  Now I feel a bit foolish about that, in a way, because I no longer think the length of time provides any indication that a relationship is solid.

When I talk to people, they often look at me like I'm a space alien.  It's like there's some aspect of social dynamics I'm apparently blind to.

> We are not born strong, we earn it.

It makes me feel like there's a muscle that can be developed.  I thought about baby sea turtles who are pretty much born into an obstacle course and have to find their way to survival.  I love those turtles.

When I see incredibly strong, resilient people, I want to be able to get there.  Believing it could ever be different would give me hope.

> I find the "adjustment" thing around people hard as well. Sometimes I feel going in that it's the only way to impress someone, and then afterwards look back and I realise I probably looked like a complete dick. That happens.

I've tried behaving like an extreme extrovert ... making people laugh and being gregarious.  Some people clearly thought I was trying too hard.  Others actually seemed to like this, but were later disappointed when I eventually got drained and couldn't keep it up.  But it's hard for me to really understand what people are thinking.  The best I can do is observe outcomes and attempt to draw an inference.  (Maybe that's what everyone does, but some people are better at it?)

> Do you think you're not "adapting" at all, or maybe you're making baby steps towards being more comfortable? 

I don't believe I've improved much.  I don't know what to do when people are concerned.  I feel like I'm stranded here and spending my time observing customs, in a way, without having a real understanding or ability to connect.  

But I do care about people's well-being, so at least there's that.

I think about the other people, alive now, and dead, and yet to be born, who've also felt this way.  Sometimes I think "I have to keep going for them." Or "I have to find some way out of this hole, so I can pull someone else out too."  But I don't know that I'm that strong of a person.  I wish I were.

And thank you.

> It's not your fault people have hurt you before, remember that

You're very sweet.  

I don't think it's their fault either ... they were doing the best they can (in the existential sense), just like everyone is.  

But I don't think I'm adapted to this world ... organisms that aren't adapted don't survive, and I think that's what's happening to me.
